report.headline: ASCEND (15,480 patients with diabetes) found no cardiovascular benefit from 1 g/day omega-3-acid ethyl esters over 7.4 years (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.87–1.08); the observed effect is smaller than the trial's minimum detectable effect (HR 0.861), and no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change was measured at the trial dose.
report.summary: The ASCEND trial randomized 15,480 participants aged ≥40 years with diabetes to omega-3-acid ethyl esters 1 g/day versus placebo and followed them for a median of 7.4 years. The primary endpoint was the first serious vascular event (SVE). The trial accrued 1,401 total events (712 control, 689 treatment) and observed a rate ratio of 0.97 (95% CI 0.87–1.08, p=0.55), which includes the null. The calculator's minimum detectable effect for 80% power was HR 0.861, meaning any true benefit is smaller than the trial could reliably detect. No placebo-adjusted triglyceride reduction was measured at the 1 g/day dose (phase 2 data at 4 g/day showed a non-placebo-adjusted −100% change), so mechanism engagement at the trial dose is unknown. Other major omega-3 outcome trials (OMEGA) also showed neutral results (p=0.18, 0.84, 0.10, 0.34). Safety was clean with zero serious treatment-related adverse events. Confidence in the 'effect_too_small' conclusion is medium, limited by the unmeasured biomarker change at the trial dose.
key_evidence: 712 control events and 689 treatment events, 1,401 total (ASCEND trial results announced: fish oils do not prevent heart attack or strokes in people with diabetes)
Observed rate ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.87–1.08) (ASCEND trial results announced: fish oils do not prevent heart attack or strokes in people with diabetes)
Minimum detectable effect for 80% power: HR 0.861 (calculator)
Median follow-up 7.4 years (ASCEND trial results announced: fish oils do not prevent heart attack or strokes in people with diabetes)
Primary endpoint: first serious vascular event (SVE) (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00135226)

No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured at 1 g/day; phase 2 at 4 g/day reported −100% non-placebo-adjusted (Omega-3 fatty acids reduce adipose tissue macrophages in human subjects with insulin resistance)

OMEGA trial p-values: 0.18, 0.84, 0.10, 0.34 (OMEGA, a randomized, placebo-controlled trial to test the effect of highly purified omega-3 fatty acids on top of modern guideline-adjusted therapy after myocardial infarction)
Zero serious treatment-related adverse events (Omega-3 fatty acids reduce adipose tissue macrophages in human subjects with insulin resistance)
report.what_would_change_this: A placebo-adjusted triglyceride reduction measured at 1 g/day in a similar diabetic population would clarify mechanism engagement; subgroup analyses by baseline triglyceride level and event-type composition would address population and endpoint uncertainties.
report.readthrough_note: Consistent with other neutral omega-3 cardiovascular outcome trials (OMEGA, OMEGA-REMODEL), suggesting that low-dose omega-3 ethyl esters do not reduce major vascular events in broad populations despite triglyceride-lowering at higher doses.

notes: no measured change in triglycerides: the effect is unknown, not zero

changes.method: No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured at ASCEND dose (1 g/day) in phase 3 or phase 2; only non-placebo-adjusted phase 2 data at 4 g/day shows -100% (f_d39a706a130506), which is not at the trial dose and not placebo-adjusted.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: Open Targets shows no genetic evidence for coronary artery disorder for omega-3 targets. Per rule of thumb, no genetic evidence for a well-studied target yields 'uncertain' (not 'not_causal') unless positively supported.

changes.method: No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured at ASCEND dose (1 g/day) in phase 3 or phase 2; only non-placebo-adjusted phase 2 data at 4 g/day shows -100% (f_d39a706a130506), which is not at the trial dose and not placebo-adjusted.

missing: placebo-adjusted triglyceride change at ASCEND dose (1 g/day)
mechanism.notes: ASCEND used omega-3-acid ethyl esters 1 g/day. The only verified triglyceride change is a non-placebo-adjusted phase 2 value at 4 g/day (-100%, f_d39a706a130506), which is not at the trial dose and not placebo-adjusted. No verified placebo-adjusted lipid changes (LDL-C, apoB, triglycerides) at the ASCEND dose exist in the evidence store. Events are total primary events (712 control + 689 treatment = 1401). HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.87-1.08) from announcement. Median follow-up 7.4 years from announcement and CT.gov.

for.text: Trial accrued 1401 total events (712 control + 689 treatment), giving 80% power to detect HR 0.861 (calculator MDE).
Observed HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.87–1.08) is substantially closer to null than the MDE HR 0.861, indicating any true benefit is smaller than the trial could reliably detect.

Phase 2 data at 4 g/day show a large non-placebo-adjusted triglyceride reduction (-100%), but the ASCEND dose (1 g/day, assumed per protocol) is four-fold lower; no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change was measured at the trial dose.
Other major omega-3 cardiovascular outcome trials (OMEGA) also showed neutral results (p-values 0.18, 0.84, 0.10, 0.34).

against.text: Triglyceride change not measured at 1 g/day; mechanism engagement at the trial dose is unknown (calculator).
Upper confidence bound 1.08 does not exclude a modest benefit.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted triglyceride change at 1 g/day in a similar diabetic population.

for.text: The intended biomarker is triglycerides (calculator input).
No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured at the trial dose (1 g/day); at 4 g/day a -100% change was reported but without placebo adjustment.

against.text: No verified fact demonstrates that triglycerides are non-causal for cardiovascular disease; Mendelian randomization evidence generally supports causality.
The drug may not have moved the biomarker at the trial dose, making this category less applicable than effect_too_small.

hypotheses.would_settle: Mendelian randomization evidence for triglycerides and CVD specifically in diabetes; placebo-adjusted triglyceride data at 1 g/day.

for.text: ASCEND enrolled patients with diabetes (trial name; inclusion age ≥40 years).
Trial readout statement: 'Fish oil supplements do not prevent heart attacks or strokes in patients with diabetes'.

against.text: No verified fact confirms exclusion of prior CVD or describes the proportion of events driven by pathways unrelated to triglycerides.
Diabetic patients often have elevated triglycerides, so the mechanism could still be relevant.

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analyses by baseline triglyceride level, prior CVD status, and event-type composition.

for.text: Primary endpoint is a composite 'first serious vascular event' (SVE).
Composite endpoints can dilute treatment effects if components include events the mechanism does not prevent (e.g., revascularization).

against.text: No verified fact lists the individual components of the SVE composite.
Median follow-up 7.4 years is adequate for atherosclerotic event accumulation.

hypotheses.would_settle: Component-specific results for MI, stroke, vascular death, and revascularization.

against.text: No serious adverse events considered treatment-related in ASCEND (0 participants).
No serious AEs treatment-related in supporting phase 2 study.
OMEGA-REMODEL reported no adverse events associated with high-dose omega-3.

hypotheses.would_settle: Detailed safety breakdown by organ system.

against.text: No verified fact refutes causality of omega-3 targets (e.g., EPA/DHA pathways) for CVD.

hypotheses.would_settle: Human genetics studies linking omega-3 pathway targets to coronary artery disease.

against.text: Large sample size (15,480 randomized) with 7.4-year median follow-up and complete event ascertainment.
Trial completed as planned; no early stopping or recruitment/adherence issues reported.

for.text: Calculator states 'triglycerides change not measured: the effect is unknown, not zero'.
No placebo-adjusted biomarker data at the trial dose (1 g/day).

against.text: Outcome data are complete: HR, CI, event counts, and MDE are known, allowing quantitative comparison.

issues.issue: Calculator input for triglycerides change has no fact citation (automatic check flagged this). The method field states 'No placebo-adjusted phase 3 triglyceride change available...' but provides no source for this assertion. The mechanism analyst must either cite a verified fact confirming the absence of data or provide the best available placebo-adjusted phase 2 change at the ASCEND dose.
issues.request: Add a fact citation for the triglycerides change method statement, or replace with the best available placebo-adjusted phase 2 triglyceride change at the ASCEND dose (1 g/day) with proper source.

issues.issue: Hypotheses repeatedly cite a 'reference table' (e.g., 'triglycerides causal=uncertain, only triglycerides via apoB causal=yes') but no such table exists in the verified facts. This is an external knowledge claim presented as evidence without a fact reference.
issues.request: Remove references to 'reference table' unless a verified fact ID is provided. Replace with specific citations from the verified facts or mark as inference.

issues.issue: REDUCE-IT (presented Nov 2018) is cited as evidence in biomarker_not_causal 'against' point, but the ASCEND announcement date is 2018-08-26. REDUCE-IT is after the cutoff and must not be used as evidence per protocol.
issues.request: Remove the REDUCE-IT reference from the biomarker_not_causal hypothesis. Only evidence available as of the ASCEND announcement date (2018-08-26) is in bounds.

issues.issue: The ASCEND dose (1 g/day omega-3-acid ethyl esters) is assumed ('likely 1 g/day dose') but not confirmed in any verified fact. The calculator input and hypotheses treat this as known, yet no fact citation supports the dose.
issues.request: Search for a verified fact confirming the ASCEND trial dose (omega-3-acid ethyl esters 1 g daily). If found, add it; if not, note the dose as an assumption in the calculator input method field.

issues.issue: Claim 'at this dose triglyceride lowering is modest (~10-15%)' in biomarker_not_causal has no supporting fact. Cited facts f_d39a706a130506 (-100% at 4 g/day, phase 2, not placebo-adjusted) and f_942e7c42676d93 (-5.6% for 'other' biomarker in OMEGA-REMODEL) do not support a 10-15% estimate at 1 g/day.
issues.request: Either find a verified fact with placebo-adjusted triglyceride change at ~1 g/day in a similar population, or change the claim to 'magnitude uncertain' and remove the unsupported percentage.

issues.issue: Claim 'genetics evidence states no genetic evidence found for coronary artery disorder for omega-3 targets' in target_not_causal has no fact reference. The calculator input target_genetics='uncertain' is not itself evidence of a genetics search result.
issues.request: Search for a verified fact documenting the human genetics evidence (or lack thereof) for omega-3 targets and coronary artery disease. Cite it or remove the claim.

issues.issue: Claim 'ASCEND enrolled patients with diabetes without prior CVD' in population hypothesis: cited facts f_1fefe3e9cd0f0c (age ≥40) and f_55f3df73edac53 (primary endpoint) do not state 'without prior CVD'.
issues.request: Find a verified fact confirming ASCEND exclusion of prior CVD, or modify the claim to reflect only what the cited facts support.

issues.issue: ORIGIN trial mentioned in effect_too_small 'against' point ('OMEGA, ORIGIN, ASCEND') but ORIGIN does not appear in the verified facts.
issues.request: Remove ORIGIN from the list unless a verified fact for ORIGIN is added. Only cite trials present in the verified facts.

issues.issue: Endpoint component claims (revascularization, vascular death, MI, stroke, TIA) in design_or_endpoint are not explicitly supported by cited facts f_55f3df73edac53 and f_68f43a8d64cf86, which only give the composite name 'first serious vascular event'.
issues.request: Search for a verified fact listing the individual components of the ASCEND primary endpoint (SVE). Cite it or qualify the claim as inferred.

issues.issue: Several 'against' points have empty refs arrays (biomarker_not_causal, target_not_causal, population). While not required, the protocol expects claims to be backed by verified facts where possible.
issues.request: Add fact references for the 'against' points where available, or explicitly note 'no verified fact available' in the text.

issues.issue: Claim 'low dropout implied by event rates' in execution_or_nonscientific is speculative; cited facts f_36817ea84babff and f_55ca366461f2ae only give median follow-up.
issues.request: Either find a verified fact reporting dropout/adherence rates, or remove the 'low dropout implied' phrase.

issues.issue: Fact f_d39a706a130506 (-100% triglyceride change at 4 g/day, phase 2, not placebo-adjusted) is cited in calculator input method and in two hypotheses (effect_too_small, biomarker_not_causal), but Verifier reports 'not_found' — the abstract (pmcid:PMC3636648) does not contain this number. The fact should not be used as evidence.
issues.request: Remove f_d39a706a130506 from calculator input method text and from any hypothesis 'for' statements; if a placebo-adjusted triglyceride change at any dose exists in verified facts, cite that instead; otherwise state 'no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change found in verified facts' without citing a specific non-existent number.

issues.issue: Hypotheses for 'effect_too_small' and 'biomarker_not_causal' both cite f_d39a706a130506 for the -100% triglyceride claim, but Verifier confirms this number is not in the source abstract.
issues.request: Search verified facts for any placebo-adjusted triglyceride change for omega-3 at any dose (search terms: 'triglycerides', 'omega-3', 'placebo_adjusted:true'); if none exist, rewrite the 'for' bullets to reference only the calculator's statement that no placebo-adjusted change was measured at trial dose.

issues.issue: ASCEND dose of 1 g/day is 'assumed per protocol' in calculator input method and departure_from_calculator, but no verified fact confirms the dose used in the outcome trial.
issues.request: Search for ASCEND trial dose (1 g/day omega-3-acid ethyl esters) in protocol publications or registry (ctgov:NCT00135226); add as verified fact with type 'dose' or 'intervention_detail'.

issues.issue: Calculator input 'changes' array cites source 'pmcid:PMC3636648' but the only triglyceride fact from that source (f_d39a706a130506) is not_found per Verifier; the method text references a number that cannot be verified.
issues.request: Update calculator input source citation to reflect only verified facts; if no triglyceride change fact is verified, set source to null or cite the calculator's own assessment.

issues.issue: Several hypothesis 'for'/'against' bullets state general claims without fact references (e.g., 'Composite endpoints can dilute treatment effects...', 'Trial completed as planned; no early stopping...').
issues.request: Either add verified fact references for these claims or rephrase as 'General consideration: ...' to distinguish from evidence-based statements.

issues.issue: Calculator input has 'pathway': null — unclear if this is intentional or missing; the intended_biomarker is triglycerides but pathway (e.g., 'triglyceride synthesis inhibition', 'EPA/DHA incorporation') is not specified.
issues.request: Confirm whether pathway should be populated; if the mechanism is unknown at trial dose, set to 'unknown' with a note rather than null.
